d03e51e375.b: Observed on Aśvinī nakshatra of Kanyā (sidereal solar) month (Prātaḥ/paraviddha).
d03e51e375.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

The 17th of the Nayanmars, Rudra Pasupathi Nayanmar, was an unparalleled devotee of Bhagavan Shiva, engaged in a specific spiritual practice involving Shri Rudram (The Yajur Veda, which is considered the Head of Bhagavan, contains seven Kandas. At the heart of the middle Kanda lies Shri Rudram, which celebrates the many magnificent manifestations of Bhagavan Shiva and is highly revered in spiritual practices). 

His method of worship included standing neck-deep in water and reciting Sri Rudram. This particular form of devotion, combining the sanctity of the scripture with the purifying nature of water, was believed to be especially potent. As a result of his deep devotion and unique practice, Rudra Pasupathi Nayanmar was graced by Bhagavan Shiva with Moksha, the liberation of the soul from the cycle of birth and death, achieving ultimate spiritual fulfillment.

d046653f0e.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in viśākhā tulā, center-to-center separation 0°59′14.78″.
d046653f0e.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°59′14.78″, 0°59′05.12″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at viśākhā-3 tulā (latitude 1°53′49.46″ N, vakra (retrograde), magnitude +2.08, elongation 10°27′48.56″ W). śukraḥ at viśākhā-3 tulā (latitude 0°54′34.68″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.92, elongation 10°19′53.81″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

d0730a64fa.d:

ಮೀನಪ್ರವೇಶೇ ಹ್ಯಮ್ಲಾನಾಂ ಮಾಲ್ಯಾನಾಮಪಿ ಚೋತ್ತಮಮ್॥  
---ಸ್ಮೃತಿಕೌಸ್ತುಭೇ  
ಸಙ್ಕ್ರಾನ್ತಿಸ್ನಾನಾಕರಣೇ ಪ್ರತ್ಯವಾಯಮಾಹ ಶಾತಾತಪಃ—  
ಸೂರ್ಯಸಙ್ಕ್ರಮಣೇ ಪುಣ್ಯೇ ನ ಸ್ನಾಯಾದ್ಯದಿ ಮಾನವಃ।  
ಸಪ್ತಜನ್ಮಸು ರೋಗೀ ಸ್ಯಾದ್ ದುಃಖಭಾಗೀ ಚ ಜಾಯತೇ॥  
ಸಙ್ಕ್ರಾನ್ತ್ಯಾಂ ಯಾನಿ ದತ್ತಾನಿ ಹವ್ಯಕವ್ಯಾನಿ ಮಾನವೈಃ।  
ತಾನಿ ತಸ್ಯ ದದಾತ್ಯರ್ಕಃ ಸಪ್ತಜನ್ಮಸು ನಿಶ್ಚಿತಮ್॥  
---ವೈದ್ಯನಾಥ-ದೀಕ್ಷಿತೀಯೇ ಸ್ಮೃತಿಮುಕ್ತಾಫಲೇ ಆಹ್ನಿಕ-ಕಾಣ್ಡಃ (ಪೂರ್ವಭಾಗಃ)  
ಷಡಶೀತ್ಯಾಂ ತು ಯದ್ದತ್ತಂ ಯದ್ದತ್ತಂ ವಿಷುವದ್ವಯೇ।  
ದೃಶ್ಯತೇ ಸಾಗರಸ್ಯಾನ್ತಸ್ತಸ್ಯಾನ್ತೋ ನೈವ ದೃಶ್ಯತೇ॥  
---ಸ್ಮೃತಿಕೌಸ್ತುಭೇ  
ಷಡಶೀತ್ಯಾಮತೀತಾಯಾಂ ಷಷ್ಟಿರುಕ್ತಾಸ್ತು ನಾಡಿಕಾಃ॥  
ಯಾ ಯಾಃ ಸನ್ನಿಹಿತಾ ನಾಡ್ಯಸ್ತಾಸ್ತಾಃ ಪುಣ್ಯತಮಾಃ ಸ್ಮೃತಾಃ॥

d26a49c830.d: The Brahmotsavam of Nataraja at Chidambaram happens specially around the Aani Thirumanjana festival each year, for ten days. On this day, Nataraja gives darshan on a Kailasha vahanam: Bhagavan Somaskanda—Shiva with Uma and Skanda—seated on Mount Kailasha as Ravananugraha-murti. In his frustration at being ignored, Ravana tried to shake the sacred mountain. Shiva subdued him with his big toe. In response, Ravana transformed one of his ten heads into a veena, using his own veins as strings, and began playing and singing praises of Shiva.

They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

In Chandra Tirtha, within the Chola kingdom, there was a sacred Shiva Lingam under a Jambu tree in a dense grove. A devout white elephant and a spider both worshiped the Lingam, but in conflicting ways. The elephant would remove the spider's web, thinking it dirtied the sacred site, while the spider spun webs to protect the Lingam from falling leaves. One day, their conflicting devotions led to a tragic end: the spider stung the elephant as it was removing the web, resulting in both their deaths.

This spider was reborn as a prince, the son of Chola king Shuba Devan and queen Kamalavati, who prayed to Bhagavan Nataraja of Chidambaram for a child. Born with red eyes due to delayed birth, he was named Kochengat Cholan. His mother passed away at his birth, and his father later retired for spiritual pursuits.

As king, Kochengat Cholan became a great patron of Shaivism. He constructed a temple at Tiru Anai Ka (now known as Tiruvanaikovil, https://maps.app.goo.gl/ZjkFyEot58UzTkNu8), at the same spot where he, as a spider, had once built webs over the Lingam. Throughout the Chola kingdom, he built numerous shrines and provided for the Brahmanas of Tillai, ensuring regular worship at Chidambaram. His contributions to Shaivism were immortalized in the poet Poygayar's work ‘Kalavazhi Narpathu’. Ultimately, Kochengat Cholan attained the divine abode of Bhagavan Shiva.

d3c2209d89.d:
The Krishna-paksha Ekadashi of vaiśākha month is known as aparā-ēkādaśī.

The fruits of fasting on Ekādaśī are greatly extolled in the Padma Purana—

A person who bathes at Śaṃkhoddhāra and beholds the image of Viṣṇu does not acquire even a sixteenth of the merit earned by fasting on Ekādaśī. O noble king, even if one gives four lakhs of coins on the days of the Sun's transition between Zodiac signs, it does not equal even a sixteenth of the merit from an Ekādaśī fast! Indeed, fasting on Ekādaśī grants the same religious merit as bathing at Prabhāsa during a lunar or solar eclipse. One who drinks the sacred water at Kedāra is freed from rebirth, and likewise, fasting on Ekādaśī removes the cycle of rebirth.

The merit from an Ekādaśī fast is a hundred times greater than the reward of performing an Ashvamedha sacrifice on earth. Fasting on Ekādaśī yields a hundredfold more merit than gifting a thousand cows to a learned brāhmaṇa. Those who fast on Ekādaśī are considered equal to those whose bodies are inhabited by Brahma, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. The merit from observing the Ekādaśī vow is immeasurable, and difficult to obtain even by the Devas. There is no other vow like that of the Ekādaśī, that destroys sins.
d3c2209d89.s:
ಅಪರಾಸೇವನಾದ್ ರಾಜನ್ ವಿಪಾಪ್ಮಾ ಭವತಿ ಧ್ರುವಮ್।  
ಕೂಟಸಾಕ್ಷ್ಯಂ ಮಾನಕೂಟಂ ತುಲಾಕೂಟಂ ಕರೋತಿ ಚ॥  
  
ಪಕ್ಷೇ ಪಕ್ಷೇ ಚ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯಾಮುಪೋಷಣಮ್।  
ಯದೀಚ್ಛೇದ್ವಿಷ್ಣುಸಾಯುಜ್ಯಂ ಶ್ರಿಯಂ ಸನ್ತತಿಮಾತ್ಮನಃ।  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯಾಂ ನ ಭುಞ್ಜೀತ ಪಕ್ಷಯೋರುಭಯೋರಪಿ॥  
  
ಅದ್ಯ ಸ್ಥಿತ್ವಾ ನಿರಾಹಾರಃ ಶ್ವೋಭೂತೇ ಪರಮೇಶ್ವರ।  
ಭೋಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಿ ಪುಣ್ಡರೀಕಾಕ್ಷ ಶರಣಂ ಮೇ ಭವಾಚ್ಯುತ॥  
ಪ್ರಮಾದಾದಥವಾಽಽಲಸ್ಯಾದ್ಧರೇ ಕೇಶವ ಮಾಧವ।  
ವ್ರತಸ್ಯಾಸ್ಯ ಚ ವೈ ವಿಘ್ನೋ ನ ಭವೇತ್ತ್ವತ್ಪ್ರಸಾದತಃ॥  
--ಪದ್ಮಪುರಾಣೇ  
  
ಶ್ರೀಬ್ರಹ್ಮವೈವರ್ತೇ ಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಖಣ್ಡೇ ಸೌತಿಶೌನಕಸಂವಾದೇ ನಾರದಂ ಪ್ರತಿ ಶಿವೋಪದೇಶೇ ಭಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಭಕ್ಷ್ಯಾದಿವಿವರಣಂ ನಾಮ ಸಪ್ತವಿಂಶತಿತಮೋಽಧ್ಯಾಯಃ---  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯಾಮನಾಹಾರಂ ಗೃಹೀ ವಿಪ್ರಶ್ಚ ಭಾರತೇ।  
ಸ ಚ ತಿಷ್ಠತಿ ವೈಕುಣ್ಠೇ ಯಾವದ್ವೈ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣೋ ವಯಃ॥೧೪॥  
  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಫಲಂ ಪ್ರೋಕ್ತಂ ಪಾದ್ಮಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ---  
ಶಙ್ಖೋದ್ಧಾರೇ ನರಃ ಸ್ನಾತ್ವಾ ದೃಷ್ಟ್ವಾ ದೇವಂ ಗದಾಧರಮ್॥೩೫॥  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಸ್ಯ ಕಲಾಂ ನಾರ್ಹತಿ ಷೋಡಶೀಮ್।  
ಸಙ್ಕ್ರಾನ್ತಿಷು ಚತುರ್ಲಕ್ಷಂ ಯೋ ದದಾತಿ ನೃಪೋತ್ತಮ॥೩೬॥  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಸ್ಯ ಕಲಾಂ ನಾರ್ಹತಿ ಷೋಡಶೀಮ್।  
ಪ್ರಭಾಸಕ್ಷೇತ್ರೇ ಯತ್ಪುಣ್ಯಂ ಗ್ರಹಣೇ ಚನ್ದ್ರಸೂರ್ಯಯೋಃ॥೩೭॥  
ತತ್ಫಲಂ ಜಾಯತೇ ನೂನಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ಕೇದಾರೇ ಚೋದಕಂ ಪೀತ್ವಾ ಪುನರ್ಜನ್ಮ ನ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ॥೩೮॥  
ತಥಾ ಚೈಕಾದಶೀ ಪಾರ್ಥ ಗರ್ಭವಾಸಕ್ಷಯಙ್ಕರೀ।  
ಅಶ್ವಮೇಧಸ್ಯ ಯಜ್ಞಸ್ಯ ಪೃಥಿವ್ಯಾಂ ಯತ್ಫಲಂ ಲಭೇತ್॥೩೯॥  
ತಸ್ಮಾಚ್ಛತಗುಣಂ ಪುಣ್ಯಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ತಪಸ್ವಿನೋ ಗೃಹೇ ಯಸ್ಯ ಭುಞ್ಜತೇ ಚ ದ್ವಿಜೋತ್ತಮಾಃ॥೪೦॥  
ತತ್ಫಲಂ ಜಾಯತೇ ನೂನಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ಗೋಸಹಸ್ರೇಣ ಯತ್ಪುಣ್ಯಂ ದತ್ವಾ ವೇದಾನ್ತಪಾರಗೇ॥೪೧॥  
ತಸ್ಮಾಚ್ಛತಗುಣಂ ಪುಣ್ಯಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ಯೇಷಾಂ ದೇಹೇ ತ್ರಯೋ ದೇವಾ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮವಿಷ್ಣುಮಹೇಶ್ವರಾಃ॥೪೨॥  
ವಸನ್ತಿ ತೇಷಾಂ ತೇ ತುಲ್ಯಾ ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ತೇ ನರಾಃ ಪುಣ್ಯಕರ್ಮಾಣೋ ಯೇ ಭಕ್ತಾ ಹರಿಪೂಜಕಾಃ॥೪೩॥  
ಏಕಾದಶೀವ್ರತಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ಪುಣ್ಯಸಙ್ಖ್ಯಾ ನ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ।  
ಏತತ್ಪುಣ್ಯಂ ಭವೇತ್ ತಸ್ಯ ಯತ್ಸುರೈರಪಿ ದುರ್ಲಭಮ್॥೪೪॥  
ಏಕಾದಶೀಸಮಂ ನಾಸ್ತಿ ವ್ರತಂ ಪಾಪಪ್ರಣಾಶನಮ್॥೧೧೮॥  
---ಶ್ರೀಪಾದ್ಮೇ ಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ ಪಞ್ಚಪಞ್ಚಾಶತ್ಸಾಹಸ್ರ್ಯಾಂ ಸಂಹಿತಾಯಾಮುತ್ತರಖಣ್ಡೇ ಉಮಾಮಹೇಶ್ವರಸಂವಾದೇ ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುತ್ಪತ್ತಿ-ಮುರವಧೋ ನಾಮ ಚತ್ವಾರಿಂಶೋಽಧ್ಯಾಯಃ॥೪೦॥

d3f974d25e.d:
Event
On 5 December, at his residence, माहेश्वर-s gathered to recite the द्राविड-स्तोत्र around him, knowing that the hour of his शिवपदप्राप्ति was fast approaching. Sporting रुद्राक्ष-s all over his person, sipping गङ्गाजल and having applied the sacred ash from चिदम्बरम्, मदुरै, काशी and तिरुचॆन्दूर्, he looked like a veritable शिवगण-नायक, who was merely in human guise on earth. At around 9 PM, he lifted his weak hands, one last time, to place upon his head as a humble salutation to the Supreme God and then gave up his last breath.

Context
Śrī Nāvalar’s last public discourse was on आडि-स्वाति of the Tamizh calendar in 1879, the गुरुपूजा of श्री-सुन्दरमूर्ति-नायनार्, the friend of महादेव. His health began to deteriorate over the next few months. The daily आत्मार्थ-पूजा he would do with so much devotion; he was unable to do it any longer and a शिवाचार्य from वेदारण्यम् would do it on his behalf.

Major celebrations
In सिंहपुरी, the गुरुपूजा of आऱुमुख-नावलर् (the day he attained शिवपद) is done without fail at शॆण्पक (चम्पक) विनायक temple every year on मघा-नक्षत्र of कार्त्तिका-मास as per the Tamizh calendar.

After the worship, he should remain awake and celebrate through songs, dances, and storytelling. Common people too should offer rice, fruits, and flowers to Bali in their homes. Whatever is done in honor of Bali brings lasting merit and pleases Viṣṇu. Viṣṇu granted Bali one day and night in the month of Kārttika to be worshipped on earth, ensuring prosperity, health, and happiness to those who observe the festival. The state of mind or action on this day—joy or sorrow—determines one’s condition for the rest of the year! d4ee398dcc.s:
ಪೂಜಾಂ ಕುರ್ಯಾತ್ತತಃ ಸಾಕ್ಷಾದ್ಭೂಮೌ ಮಣ್ಡಲಕೇ ಕೃತೇ।  
ಬಲಿಮಾಲಿಖ್ಯ ದೈತ್ಯೇನ್ದ್ರಂ ವರ್ಣಕೈಃ ಪಞ್ಚರಙ್ಗಕೈಃ॥೩೯॥  
ಸರ್ವಾಭರಣಸಮ್ಪೂರ್ಣಂ ವಿನ್ಧ್ಯಾವಲಿಸಮನ್ವಿತಮ್।  
ಕೂಷ್ಮಾಣ್ಡಮಯಜಮ್ಭೋರುಮಧುದಾನವಸಂವೃತಮ್॥೪೦॥  
ಸಮ್ಪೂರ್ಣಂ ಕೃಷ್ಟವದನಂ ಕಿರೀಟೋತ್ಕಟಕುಣ್ಡಲಮ್।  
ದ್ವಿಭುಜಂ ದೈತ್ಯರಾಜಾನಂ ಕಾರಯಿತ್ವಾ ಸ್ವಕೇ ಪುನಃ॥೪೧॥  
ಗೃಹಸ್ಯ ಮಧ್ಯೇ ಶಾಲಾಯಾಂ ವಿಶಾಲಾಯಾಂ ತತೋಽರ್ಚಯೇತ್।  
ಮಾತೃಭ್ರಾತೃಜನೈಃ ಸಾರ್ಧಂ ಸನ್ತುಷ್ಟೋ ಬನ್ಧುಭಿಃ ಸಹ॥೪೨॥  
ಕಮಲೈಃ ಕುಮುದೈಃ ಪುಷ್ಪೈಃ ಕಹ್ಲಾರೈ ರಕ್ತಕೋತ್ಪಲೈಃ।  
ಗನ್ಧಪುಷ್ಪಾನ್ನನೈವೇದ್ಯೈಃ ಸಕ್ಷೀರೈರ್ಗುಡಪಾಯಸೈಃ॥೪೩॥  
ಮದ್ಯಮಾಂಸಸುರಾಲೇಹ್ಯಚೋಷ್ಯಭಕ್ಷ್ಯೋಪಹಾರಕೈಃ।  
ಮನ್ತ್ರೇಣಾನೇನ ರಾಜೇನ್ದ್ರ ಸಮನ್ತ್ರೀ ಸಪುರೋಹಿತಃ।  
ಪೂಜಾಂ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತೇ ಯೋ ವೈ ಸೌಖ್ಯಂ ಸ್ಯಾತ್ತಸ್ಯ ವತ್ಸರಮ್॥೪೪॥  
**ಬಲಿರಾಜ ನಮತುಭ್ಯಂ ವಿರೋಚನಸುತ ಪ್ರಭೋ।  
ಭವಿಷ್ಯೇನ್ದ್ರ ಸುರಾರಾತೇ ಪೂಜೇಯಂ ಪ್ರತಿಗೃಹ್ಯತಾಮ್॥೪೫॥**  
ಏವಂ ಪೂಜಾವಿಧಾನೇನ ರಾತ್ರೌ ಜಾಗರಣಂ ತತಃ।  
ಕಾರಯೇದ್ವೈ ಕ್ಷಣಂ ರಾತ್ರೌ ನಟನೃತ್ಯಕಥಾನಕೈಃ॥೪೬॥  
ಲೋಕಶ್ಚಾಪಿ ಗೃಹಸ್ಯಾನ್ತೇ ಸಪರ್ಯಾಂ ಶುಕ್ಲತಣ್ಡುಲೈಃ।  
ಸಂಸ್ಥಾಪ್ಯ ಬಲಿರಾಜಾನಂ ಫಲೈಃ ಪುಷ್ಪೈಃ ಪ್ರಪೂಜಯೇತ್॥೪೭॥  
ಬಲಿಮುದ್ದಿಶ್ಯ ವೈ ತತ್ರ ಕಾರ್ಯಂ ಸರ್ವಂ ಚ ಸುವ್ರತ।  
ಯಾನಿ ಯಾನ್ಯಕ್ಷಯಾಣ್ಯಾಹುರ್ಮುನಯಸ್ತತ್ತ್ವದರ್ಶಿನಃ॥೪೮॥  
ಯದತ್ರ ದೀಯತೇ ದಾನಂ ಸ್ವಲ್ಪಂ ವಾ ಯದಿ ವಾ ಬಹು।  
ತದಕ್ಷಯಂ ಭವೇತ್ಸರ್ವಂ ವಿಷ್ಣೋಃ ಪ್ರೀತಿಕರಂ ಶುಭಮ್॥೪೯॥  
ರಾತ್ರೌ ಯೇ ನ ಕರಿಷ್ಯನ್ತಿ ತವ ಪೂಜಾಂ ಬಲೇ ನರಾಃ।  
ತೇಷಾಂ ಚ ಶ್ರೋತ್ರಿಯೋ ಧರ್ಮಃ ಸರ್ವಸ್ತ್ವಾಮುಪತಿಷ್ಠತು॥೫೦॥  
ವಿಷ್ಣುನಾ ಚ ಸ್ವಯಂ ವತ್ಸ ತುಷ್ಟೇನ ಬಲಯೇ ಪುನಃ।  
ಉಪಕಾರಕರಂ ದತ್ತಮಸುರಾಣಾಂ ಮಹೋತ್ಸವಮ್॥೫೧॥  
ಏಕಮೇವಮಹೋರಾತ್ರಂ ವರ್ಷೇ ವರ್ಷೇ ಚ ಕಾರ್ತಿಕೇ।  
ದತ್ತಂ ದಾನವರಾಜಸ್ಯ ಆದರ್ಶಮಿವ ಭೂತಲೇ॥೫೨॥  
ಯಃ ಕರೋತಿ ನೃಪೋ ರಾಜ್ಯೇ ತಸ್ಯ ವ್ಯಾಧಿಭಯಂ ಕುತಃ।  
ಸುಭಿಕ್ಷಂ ಕ್ಷೇಮಮಾರೋಗ್ಯಂ ತಸ್ಯ ಸಮ್ಪದನುತ್ತಮಾ॥೫೩॥  
ನೀರುಜಶ್ಚ ಜನಾಃ ಸರ್ವೇ ಸರ್ವೋಪದ್ರವವರ್ಜಿತಾಃ॥೫೪॥  
ಕೌಮುದೀ ಕ್ರಿಯತೇ ಯಸ್ಮಾದ್ಭಾವಂ ಕರ್ತುಂ ಮಹೀತಲೇ।  
ಯೋ ಯಾದೃಶೇನ ಭಾವೇನ ತಿಷ್ಠತ್ಯಸ್ಯಾಂ ಚ ಸುವ್ರತ।  
ಹರ್ಷದುಃಖಾದಿಭಾವೇನ ತಸ್ಯ ವರ್ಷಂ ಪ್ರಯಾತಿ ಹಿ॥೫೫॥  
ರುದಿತೇ ರೋದಿತಂ ವರ್ಷಂ ಪ್ರಹೃಷ್ಟೇ ತು ಪ್ರಹರ್ಷಿತಮ್।  
ಭುಕ್ತೌ ಭೋಗ್ಯಂ ಭವೇದ್ವರ್ಷಂ ಸ್ವಸ್ಥೇ ಸ್ವಸ್ಥಂ ಭವಿಷ್ಯತಿ॥೫೬॥  
ವೈಷ್ಣವೀ ದಾನವೀ ಚೇಯಂ ತಿಥಿಃ ಪ್ರೋಕ್ತಾ ಚ ಕಾರ್ತಿಕೇ॥೫೭॥  
ದೀಪೋತ್ಸವಂ ಜನಿತಸರ್ವಜನಪ್ರಮೋದಂ  
ಕುರ್ವನ್ತಿ ಯೇ ಶುಭತಯಾ ಬಲಿರಾಜಪೂಜಾಮ್।  
ದಾನೋಪಭೋಗಸುಖಬುದ್ಧಿಮತಾಂ ಕುಲಾನಾಂ  
ಹರ್ಷಂ ಪ್ರಯಾತಿ ಸಕಲಂ ಪ್ರಮುದಾ ಚ ವರ್ಷಮ್॥೫೮॥  
ಬಲಿಪೂಜಾಂ ವಿಧಾಯೈವಂ ಪಶ್ಚಾದ್ಗೋಕ್ರೀಡನಂ ಚರೇತ್॥೫೯॥  
—ಇತಿ ಶ್ರೀಸ್ಕಾನ್ದೇ ಮಹಾಪುರಾಣ ಏಕಾಶೀತಿಸಾಹಸ್ರ್ಯಾಂ ಸಂಹಿತಾಯಾಂ ದ್ವಿತೀಯೇ ವೈಷ್ಣವಖಣ್ಡೇ ಕಾರ್ತಿಕಮಾಸಮಾಹಾತ್ಮ್ಯೇ ಕಾರ್ತಿಕಶುಕ್ಲಪ್ರತಿಪನ್ಮಾಹಾತ್ಮ್ಯವರ್ಣನಂ ನಾಮ ದಶಮೋಽಧ್ಯಾಯಃ॥೧೦॥

d5347b4be8.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in śravaṇaḥ makaraḥ, center-to-center separation 0°41′09.77″.
d5347b4be8.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°41′09.77″, 0°41′02.40″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at śravaṇaḥ-4 makaraḥ (latitude 2°00′25.41″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.28, elongation 5°47′39.14″ E). śukraḥ at śravaṇaḥ-4 makaraḥ (latitude 1°19′15.64″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.91, elongation 5°35′39.98″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.
d5347b4be8.s:

Coming from Brahma's Kamandalu, Pushkara Raja resides in different rivers, along with 3.5 crore tirthas, following the Sankranti of Guru, for twelve days at the beginning of the Sankranti (ādya puṣkaram) and at the end of the year (preceding transition to the next rāśī, antya puṣkaram), and for two muhurtas during mid-day, every day, during the entire year.

d537cfec66.s:
ಮೇಷೇ ಚ ಗಙ್ಗಾ ವೃಷಭೇ ಚ ನರ್ಮದಾ ಯುಗ್ಮೇ ಚ ವಾಣೀ ಯಮುನಾ ಕುಲೀರೇ  
ಗೋದಾವರೀ ಸಿಂಹಗತೇ ಚ ಕನ್ಯಾಙ್ಗತೇ ದೇವಗುರೌ ಚ ಕೃಷ್ಣಾ।  
ಕಾವೇರೀ ತೌಲ್ಯಾಂ ಅಲಿತಾಮ್ರಪರ್ಣೀ ಚಾಪೇ ಚ ಸಿನ್ಧು ಮಕರೇ ಚ ಭದ್ರಾ  
ಘಟೇ ಗುರೌ ಭೀಮರಥೀ ಪ್ರಣೀತಾ ಮೀನೇ ಗತೇ ಪುಷ್ಕರಮಾಹುರಾರ್ಯಾಃ॥  
ಯದಾ ರಾಶಿ-ಪ್ರವೇಶಃ ಸ್ಯಾತ್ತದಾ ಪ್ರಭೃತಿ ಸರ್ವದಾ।  
ದ್ವಾದಶಾಹಮಿತೇ ಕಾಲೇ ವಸ್ತವ್ಯಂ ತು ಮಮಾಽಽಜ್ಞಯಾ॥  
ಆವತ್ಸರಂ ತು ವಸ್ತವ್ಯಂ ಮಧ್ಯಾಹ್ನೇ ದ್ವಿಮುಹೂರ್ತಕಮ್।  
ಅನ್ತೇ ದ್ವಾದಶ ವಸ್ತವ್ಯಂ ದಿನಾನಿ ಚ ಯಥಾಸುಖಮ್॥

ಅಥಾಶ್ವಿನಶುಕ್ಲಪ್ರತಿಪದಿ ದೌಹಿತ್ರೇಣ ಮಾತಾಮಹಶ್ರಾದ್ಧಂ ಕಾರ್ಯಮ್॥  
ತದುಕ್ತಂ ಹೇಮಾದ್ರೌ---  
ಜಾತಮಾತ್ರೋಽಪಿ ದೌಹಿತ್ರೋ ಜೀವತ್ಯಪಿ ಚ ಮಾತುಲೇ।  
ಕುರ್ಯಾನ್ಮಾತಾಮಹಶ್ರಾದ್ಧಂ ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಾಶ್ವಿನೇ ಸಿತೇ॥  
ಇಯಂ ಚ ಸಙ್ಗವವ್ಯಾಪಿನೀ ಗ್ರಾಹ್ಯೇತಿ ನಿರ್ಣಯದೀಪೇ ಉಕ್ತಮ್॥  
ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಾಶ್ವಿನ ಶುಕ್ಲೇ ದೌಹಿತ್ರಸ್ತ್ವೇಕಪಾರ್ವಣಮ್।  
ಶ್ರಾದ್ಧಂ ಮಾತಾಮಹಂ ಕುರ್ಯಾತ್ ಸಪಿತಾ ಸಙ್ಗವೇ ಸತಿ॥  
ಜಾತಮಾತ್ರೋಽಪಿ ದೌಹಿತ್ರೋ ಜೀವತ್ಯಪಿ ಹಿ ಮಾತುಲೇ।  
ಪ್ರಾತಃ ಸಙ್ಗವಯೋರ್ಮಧ್ಯೇ ಯಾಽಶ್ವಯುಕ್ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ ಭವೇತ್॥  
ಅತ್ರ ಸಪಿತಾ ಇತಿ ವಿಶೇಷಣಾಜ್ಜೀವತ್ಪಿತೃಕ ಏವಾಧಿಕಾರೀ ಪಿಣ್ಡರಹಿತಂ ಕುರ್ಯಾತ್॥  
ಮುಣ್ಡನಂ ಪಿಣ್ಡದಾನಂ ಚ ಪ್ರೇತಕರ್ಮ ಚ ಸರ್ವಶಃ।  
ನ ಜೀವತ್ಪಿತೃಕಃ ಕುರ್ಯಾದ್ಗುರ್ವಿಣೀಪತಿರೇವ ಚ॥   
ಇತಿ ಪಿಣ್ಡನಿಷೇಧಾತ್॥

d5da1ccf9c.b: Observed on Citrā nakshatra of Mēṣaḥ (sidereal solar) month (Prātaḥ/paraviddha).
d5da1ccf9c.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

In the region of Tirunavalur in Tirumuraipadi, there lived a devout Adi Shaiva named Sadayanar, whose lineage was known for its deep devotion to Bhagavan Shiva. Sadayanar, embodying the same piety and dedication, was married to Isaijnaniyar, a woman equally devoted to Bhagavan. Their virtuous past actions blessed them with a divine child, who was none other than Sundaramurthi Nayanmar.

The child's striking beauty caught the attention of Narasinga Munaiyar, the local king, who expressed a desire to raise the child himself. Demonstrating their detachment from worldly attachments, Sadayanar and Isaijnaniyar willingly entrusted their child to the king without hesitation. This couple exemplified the ideal life of householders, focusing on spiritual devotion and ultimately earning the grace of the Divine.
d5da1ccf9c.r: - 63 Nayanmar Saints by Swami Sivananda, published by The Divine Life Society

By rashi: karkaṭaḥ, siṁhaḥ, dhanuḥ, mēṣaḥ get more ashubha phala, vr̥śchikaḥ, makaraḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam somewhat ashubha, kanyā, tulā, kumbhaḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ shubha phala. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.

Preceptor Surendra, a Maharashtrian, revered by all as Māthura, resorted to asceticism, an adept in Yogic practices, governed the Maṭha for only ten years and reached his abode on the first day of the bright fortnight in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa of the Tāraṇa year in the Kali era 3486.
d64bc7034e.s:
ದುರ್ದೀದಿವಿಂ ಸಮಭಿಭೂಯ ತಥಾಽಸ್ಯ ಸಾಹ್ಯಾ-  
ಸಕ್ತಂ ಚ ಜೀವಮಪವಾರ್ಯ ಸಧೈರ್ಯಮುಕ್ತ್ಯಾ।  
ಸಮ್ಪೂಜಿತಃ ಸದಸಿ ರಾಜಸುರೇನ್ದ್ರಮುಖ್ಯೈಃ  
ಯೋಗೀ ಸುರೇನ್ದ್ರನಿಯಮೀ ಯುಯುಜೇ ಪದೇ ಸ್ವೇ॥೩೯॥  
ಮಹಾರಾಷ್ಟ್ರಃ ಸರ್ವೈರಪಿ ಚ ವಿನುತೋ ಮಾಥುರ ಇತಿ

ದಶೈವಾಧ್ಯುಷ್ಯಾಬ್ದಾನ್ ಅಧಿಮಠಮಯಂ ಯೋಗಿತಿಲಕಃ  
ಸುರೇನ್ದ್ರಃ ಸ್ವಂ ಮಾರ್ಗೇ ಪ್ರತಿಪದಿ ಸಿತೇ ಪ್ರಾಪ ನಿಲಯಮ್॥೪೦॥

---ನಿರ್ಣಯಸಿನ್ಧುಃ  
ತುಲಾಪ್ರವೇಶೇ ಧಾನ್ಯಾನಾಂ ಬೀಜಾನಾಮೇವ ಚೋತ್ತಮಮ್॥  
---ಸ್ಮೃತಿಕೌಸ್ತುಭೇ  
ಸಙ್ಕ್ರಾನ್ತಿಸ್ನಾನಾಕರಣೇ ಪ್ರತ್ಯವಾಯಮಾಹ ಶಾತಾತಪಃ—  
ಸೂರ್ಯಸಙ್ಕ್ರಮಣೇ ಪುಣ್ಯೇ ನ ಸ್ನಾಯಾದ್ಯದಿ ಮಾನವಃ।

ಸಙ್ಕ್ರಾನ್ತ್ಯಾಂ ಯಾನಿ ದತ್ತಾನಿ ಹವ್ಯಕವ್ಯಾನಿ ಮಾನವೈಃ।  
ತಾನಿ ತಸ್ಯ ದದಾತ್ಯರ್ಕಃ ಸಪ್ತಜನ್ಮಸು ನಿಶ್ಚಿತಮ್॥  
---ವೈದ್ಯನಾಥ-ದೀಕ್ಷಿತೀಯೇ ಸ್ಮೃತಿಮುಕ್ತಾಫಲೇ ಆಹ್ನಿಕ-ಕಾಣ್ಡಃ (ಪೂರ್ವಭಾಗಃ)

d95e4fe382.d:
Beginning of Dhanurmasa puja in temples and at homes. A very early morning puja is performed, typically with mudgānnam as naivedyam. Begets fruit equivalent to performing puja for a thousand years!
The two ayana-s of the Sun are night and day for the Devas. 30 of these days become a month. The uṣahkāla of their day starts in chāpamāsa i.e. dhanurmāsa (although the shloka refers to the sidereal month, it appears logical to use the tropical month, owing to its association with uttarāyaṇam). Therefore, one must strive to perform uṣahkāla-pujā in this month, before sunrise --- a ṣōḍaśōpachāra-pūjā. Following this, one must perform Sandhyavandam and upasthanam! The Shivapurana also extols the uniqueness of the early morning puja in this month, suggesting that one must perform rudrābhiṣeka.
d95e4fe382.s:
ಭಾಸ್ಕರೀಯೇ---  
ಅಯನಂ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ ರಾತ್ರಿರುತ್ತರಂ ತು ದಿವಾ ಭವೇತ್।  
ದೈವತಂ ತದಹೋರಾತ್ರಂ ತತ್ ತ್ರಿಂಶನ್ಮಾಸ ಉಚ್ಯತೇ॥  
ತದ್ದಿನಸ್ಯ ಉಷಃಕಾಲಂ ಚಾಪಮಾಸಂ ವಿದುರ್ಬುಧಾಃ।  
ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಯತ್ನೇನ ಚಾಪಮಾಸೇ ದಿನೇ ದಿನೇ॥  
ಉಷಃಕಾಲೇ ತು ಸಮ್ಪ್ರಾಪ್ತೇ ಬೋಧಯಿತ್ವಾ ಜನಾರ್ದನಮ್।  
ಸಮಭ್ಯರ್ಚ್ಯ ಭಜೇದ್ವಿಷ್ಣುಂ ಜನಾನಾಂ ದೋಷಶಾನ್ತಯೇ॥  
ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಾಣ್ಡಪುರಾಣೇ---  
ಉಷಃಕಾಲೇ ತು ಸಮ್ಪ್ರಾಪ್ತೇ ಅರ್ಚಯಿತ್ವಾ ಜನಾರ್ದನಮ್।  
ಉಪಚಾರೈಃ ಷೋಡಶಭಿರ್ಮುದ್ಗಾನ್ನಂ ಚ ನಿವೇದಯೇತ್॥  
ಆದಿತ್ಯ ಪುರಾಣೇ---  
ಉಷಃಕಾಲೇ ತು ಸಮ್ಪ್ರಾಪ್ತೇ ಪ್ರತ್ಯೂಷೇ ಸ್ನಾನಮಾಚರೇತ್।  
ಅರ್ಚಯೇಚ್ಚ ಜಗನ್ನಾಥಂ ಯಾವತ್ಸೂರ್ಯೋದಯಾತ್ಪುರಾ॥  
ತತಃ ಪ್ರಭಾತಸಮಯೇ ಅರ್ಘ್ಯಂ ಪ್ರಕ್ಷಿಪ್ಯ ವೈ ದ್ವಿಜಃ।  
ಗಾಯತ್ರೀಂ ಚ ತತೋ ಜಪ್ತ್ವಾ ಉಪತಿಷ್ಠೇತ ಭಾಸ್ಕರಮ್॥  
ಶಿವಪುರಾಣೇ---  
ಚಾಪರಾಶೌ ಸ್ಥಿತೇ ಸೂರ್ಯೇ ಉಷಃಕಾಲೇ ದಿನೇ ದಿನೇ।  
ಅಭಿಷೇಕಂ ತತಃ ಕುರ್ಯಾದ್ರೌದ್ರಮನ್ತ್ರೇಣ ರುದ್ರವಿತ್॥  
ಅರ್ಕಪುಷ್ಪೈಶ್ಚ ಬಿಲ್ವೈಶ್ಚ ಪೂಜಯೇಚ್ಚ ಮಹೇಶ್ವರಮ್।  
ನೈವೇದ್ಯಂ ಚ ತತಃ ಕುರ್ಯಾತ್ ಲೋಕಸಂಹಾರ ಶಾನ್ತಯೇ॥  
ಅನ್ಯತ್ರ---  
ಕೋದಣ್ಡಸ್ಥೇ ಸವಿತರಿ ಪ್ರತ್ಯೂಷೇ ಪೂಜಯೇದ್ಧರೇಃ।  
ಸಹಸ್ರಾಬ್ದಾರ್ಚನಫಲಂ ದಿನೇನೈಕೇನ ಲಭ್ಯತೇ॥

This marks the tenth day of the festival. This is the day of the chariot/car festival.

da7c320dfc.d:
The Krishna-paksha Ekadashi of kārttika month is known as utpannā-ēkādaśī. Yudhiṣṭhira inquires about the origin of the auspicious Ekādaśī day and its importance in the universe, especially for the deities. In response, Bhagavan Viṣṇu narrates a story from the Kṛta yuga about a fierce demon named Mura, who terrorized the Devas, even defeating Indra and forcing them to flee from Svarga. Seeking help, Indra and the Devas approached Bhagavan Śiva, who directed them to Bhagavan Viṣṇu, the protector. The Devas, led by Indra, found Bhagavan Viṣṇu asleep in the water and pleaded for his help. Bhagavan Viṣṇu inquired about the demon, and Indra explained Mura's origins, his strength, and how he had created an alternate realm of Devas and occupied Svarga. Enraged, Bhagavan Viṣṇu vowed to defeat Mura and attacked his forces. Though many demons were killed, Mura proved to be a formidable opponent, leading to a protracted battle with Bhagavan Viṣṇu that lasted a thousand divine years. Eventually, exhausted, Bhagavan Viṣṇu retreated to the cave of Siṃhavatī in Badarikāśrama to rest. Mura pursued him, believing he had won. As Bhagavan Viṣṇu slept, Mura prepared to kill him. At that moment, a divine maiden, born from Bhagavan Viṣṇu's radiance, appeared and challenged Mura. In a fierce battle, the maiden, using her divine powers, defeated Mura and reduced him to ash with a single powerful sound. When Bhagavan Viṣṇu awoke, he was astonished to find Mura defeated and asked the maiden how she had accomplished this feat. She explained that she killed Mura to protect the world while Bhagavan Viṣṇu slept. Bhagavan Viṣṇu, impressed, offered her a boon. The maiden, who identified herself as Ekādaśī, requested to be the most auspicious of days, granting all those who fast in her honor health, wealth, righteousness, and ultimately, salvation. Bhagavan Viṣṇu granted her wish, decreeing that Ekādaśī would become the holiest day, capable of destroying all sins and conferring (even) salvation to those who observe it. Thus came about the birth of Ekādaśī and the Ekādaśī vrata itself---thus, this day in Kartika is known by the name of utpannā, i.e. birth.

The fruits of fasting on Ekādaśī are greatly extolled in the Padma Purana—

A person who bathes at Śaṃkhoddhāra and beholds the image of Viṣṇu does not acquire even a sixteenth of the merit earned by fasting on Ekādaśī. O noble king, even if one gives four lakhs of coins on the days of the Sun's transition between Zodiac signs, it does not equal even a sixteenth of the merit from an Ekādaśī fast! Indeed, fasting on Ekādaśī grants the same religious merit as bathing at Prabhāsa during a lunar or solar eclipse. One who drinks the sacred water at Kedāra is freed from rebirth, and likewise, fasting on Ekādaśī removes the cycle of rebirth.

The merit from an Ekādaśī fast is a hundred times greater than the reward of performing an Ashvamedha sacrifice on earth. Fasting on Ekādaśī yields a hundredfold more merit than gifting a thousand cows to a learned brāhmaṇa. Those who fast on Ekādaśī are considered equal to those whose bodies are inhabited by Brahma, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. The merit from observing the Ekādaśī vow is immeasurable, and difficult to obtain even by the Devas. There is no other vow like that of the Ekādaśī, that destroys sins.
da7c320dfc.s:
ಪಕ್ಷೇ ಪಕ್ಷೇ ಚ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯಾಮುಪೋಷಣಮ್।  
ಯದೀಚ್ಛೇದ್ವಿಷ್ಣುಸಾಯುಜ್ಯಂ ಶ್ರಿಯಂ ಸನ್ತತಿಮಾತ್ಮನಃ।  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯಾಂ ನ ಭುಞ್ಜೀತ ಪಕ್ಷಯೋರುಭಯೋರಪಿ॥  
  
ಅದ್ಯ ಸ್ಥಿತ್ವಾ ನಿರಾಹಾರಃ ಶ್ವೋಭೂತೇ ಪರಮೇಶ್ವರ।  
ಭೋಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಿ ಪುಣ್ಡರೀಕಾಕ್ಷ ಶರಣಂ ಮೇ ಭವಾಚ್ಯುತ॥  
ಪ್ರಮಾದಾದಥವಾಽಽಲಸ್ಯಾದ್ಧರೇ ಕೇಶವ ಮಾಧವ।  
ವ್ರತಸ್ಯಾಸ್ಯ ಚ ವೈ ವಿಘ್ನೋ ನ ಭವೇತ್ತ್ವತ್ಪ್ರಸಾದತಃ॥  
--ಪದ್ಮಪುರಾಣೇ  
  
ಶ್ರೀಬ್ರಹ್ಮವೈವರ್ತೇ ಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಖಣ್ಡೇ ಸೌತಿಶೌನಕಸಂವಾದೇ ನಾರದಂ ಪ್ರತಿ ಶಿವೋಪದೇಶೇ ಭಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಭಕ್ಷ್ಯಾದಿವಿವರಣಂ ನಾಮ ಸಪ್ತವಿಂಶತಿತಮೋಽಧ್ಯಾಯಃ---  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯಾಮನಾಹಾರಂ ಗೃಹೀ ವಿಪ್ರಶ್ಚ ಭಾರತೇ।  
ಸ ಚ ತಿಷ್ಠತಿ ವೈಕುಣ್ಠೇ ಯಾವದ್ವೈ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣೋ ವಯಃ॥೧೪॥  
  
ಯುಧಿಷ್ಠಿರ ಉವಾಚ---  
ಉತ್ಪನ್ನಾ ಸಾ ಕಥಂ ದೇವ ಪುಣ್ಯಾ ಚೈಕಾದಶೀ ತಿಥಿಃ।  
ಕಥಂ ಪವಿತ್ರಾ ವಿಶ್ವೇಽಸ್ಮಿನ್ಕಥಂ ವೈ ದೇವತಾಪ್ರಿಯಾ॥೪೯॥  
ಶ್ರೀಭಗವಾನುವಾಚ---  
ಪುರಾ ಕೃತಯುಗೇ ಪಾರ್ಥ ಮುರನಾಮೇತಿ ದಾನವಃ।  
ಅತ್ಯದ್ಭುತೋ ಮಹಾರೌದ್ರಃ ಸರ್ವದೇವಭಯಙ್ಕರಃ॥೫೦॥  
...  
ಪ್ರಸುಪ್ತಂ ತತ್ರ ಮಾಂ ದೃಷ್ಟ್ವಾ ದಾನವೋ ಹರ್ಷಮಾಗತಃ॥೮೩॥  
ಇತ್ಥಂ ಮಾಂ ನಿರ್ಜಿತಂ ಮತ್ವಾ ಪ್ರವಿಷ್ಟಂ ಶಙ್ಕಯಾ ಹರಿಮ್।  
ನಿಃಸನ್ದೇಹಂ ಹನಿಷ್ಯಾಮಿ ದಾನವಾನಾಂ ಭಯಙ್ಕರಮ್॥೮೪॥  
ನಿರ್ಗತಾ ಕನ್ಯಕಾ ತತ್ರ ವಿಷ್ಣುದೇಹಾದ್ಯುಧಿಷ್ಠಿರ।  
ರೂಪವತೀ ಸುಸೌಭಾಗ್ಯಾ ದಿವ್ಯಪ್ರಹರಣಾಯುಧಾ॥೮೫॥  
ತಸ್ಯ ತೇಜೋಂಽಶಸಮ್ಭೂತಾ ಮಹಾಬಲಪರಾಕ್ರಮಾ।  
ದೃಷ್ಟಾ ಸಾ ದಾನವೇನ್ದ್ರೇಣ ಮುರನಾಮ್ನಾ ಯುಧಿಷ್ಠಿರ॥೮೬॥  
ಯುದ್ಧಂ ಸಮಾಹಿತಂ ತೇನ ಸ್ತ್ರಿಯಾ ಚೈವ ಪ್ರಯಾಚಿತಮ್।  
ಕನ್ಯಕಾ ಯುಧ್ಯತೇ ತತ್ರ ಸರ್ವಯುದ್ಧವಿಶಾರದಾ॥೮೭॥  
ಹುಙ್ಕಾರೈರ್ಭಸ್ಮಸಾಜ್ಜಾತೋ ಮುರನಾಮಾ ಮಹಾಸುರಃ।  
ನಿಹತೇ ದಾನವೇ ತಸ್ಮಿಂಸ್ತತ್ರ ದೇವಸ್ತ್ವಬುಧ್ಯತ॥೮೮॥  
ಪತಿತಂ ದಾನವಂ ದೃಷ್ಟ್ವಾ ತತೋ ವಿಸ್ಮಯಮಾಗತಃ।  
ಕೇನಾಯಂ ಚ ಹತೋ ರೌದ್ರೋ ಹ್ಯತ್ಯುಗ್ರೋ ಮಮ ಶತ್ರುಕಃ॥೮೯॥  
ಅತ್ಯುಗ್ರಂ ಚ ಕೃತಂ ಕರ್ಮ ಮಮ ಕಾರುಣ್ಯತಾ ಕೃತಮ್।  
ಕನ್ಯೋವಾಚ---  
ತೇನ ದೇವಾಶ್ಚ ಗನ್ಧರ್ವಾಃ ಸಯಕ್ಷೋರಗರಾಕ್ಷಸಾಃ॥೯೦॥  
ಇನ್ದ್ರಾದ್ಯಾಃ ಸಕಲಾ ಜಿತ್ವಾ ಸ್ವರ್ಗಾಚ್ಚೈವ ನಿರಾಕೃತಾಃ।  
ಹರಿಃ ಸುಪ್ತೋ ಮಯಾ ದೃಷ್ಟೋ ಮುರಃ ಪೃಷ್ಠೇ ಸಮಾಗತಃ॥೯೧॥  
ಸಂಹರಿಷ್ಯತಿ ತ್ರೈಲೋಕ್ಯಂ ಸುಪ್ತೇ ಚೈವ ಜರ್ನಾದನೇ।  
ಶ್ರೀಕೃಷ್ಣ ಉವಾಚ---  
ತಸ್ಯಾಸ್ತದ್ವಚನಂ ಶ್ರುತ್ವಾ ವಿಷ್ಣುರ್ವಚನಮಬ್ರವೀತ್॥೯೨॥  
ಶ್ರೀವಿಷ್ಣುರುವಾಚ---  
ಅಹಂ ಚ ನಿರ್ಜಿತೋ ಯೇನ ಕಥಂ ಸೋಽಪಿ ತ್ವಯಾ ಜಿತಃ।  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುವಾಚ---  
ತ್ವತ್ಪ್ರಸಾದಾಚ್ಚ ಭೋಃ ಸ್ವಾಮಿನ್ಮಹಾದೈತ್ಯೋ ಮಯಾ ಹತಃ॥೯೩॥  
ಶ್ರೀಭಗವಾನುವಾಚ---  
ಆನನ್ದಂ ತ್ರಿಷು ಲೋಕೇಷು ಮುನಯೋ ದೇವತಾ ಗತಾಃ।  
ಬ್ರೂಹಿ ತ್ವಂ ಚ ಮಯಾ ಭದ್ರೇ ಯತ್ತೇ ಮನಸಿ ರೋಚತೇ।  
ದದಾಮಿ ಚ ನ ಸನ್ದೇಹೋ ಯತ್ಸುರೈರಪಿ ದುರ್ಲಭಮ್॥೯೪॥  
...  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುವಾಚ---  
ತ್ರಿಭುವನೇಷು ಚ ದೇವೇಶ ಚತುರ್ಯುಗೇಷು ಸಾಮ್ಪ್ರತಮ್।  
ತ್ರಿಷು ಲೋಕೇಷು ಸರ್ವತ್ರ ತಾದೃಶಂ ಕುರು ಮೇ ಪ್ರಭೋ॥೯೮॥  
ಸರ್ವತೀರ್ಥಪ್ರಧಾನಂ ಹಿ ಸರ್ವವಿಘ್ನವಿನಾಶಿನೀ।  
ಸರ್ವಸಿದ್ಧಿಕರೀ ದೇವೀ ತ್ವತ್ಪ್ರಸಾದಾದ್ಭವಾಮ್ಯಹಮ್॥೯೯॥  
ಮಾಮುಪೋಷ್ಯನ್ತಿ ಯೇ ಭಕ್ತ್ಯಾ ತವ ಭಕ್ತ್ಯಾ ಜನಾರ್ದನ।  
ಸರ್ವಸಿದ್ಧಿರ್ಭವೇತ್ತೇಷಾಂ ಯದಿ ತುಷ್ಟೋಽಸಿ ಮೇ ಪ್ರಭೋ॥೧೦೦॥  
ಉಪವಾಸಂ ಚ ನಕ್ತಂ ಚ ಏಕಭಕ್ತಂ ಕರೋತಿ ಚ।  
ತಸ್ಯ ವಿತ್ತಂ ಚ ಧರ್ಮಂ ಚ ಮೋಕ್ಷಂ ವೈ ದೇಹಿ ಮಾಧವ॥೧೦೧॥  
ವಿಷ್ಣುರುವಾಚ---  
ಯತ್ತ್ವಂ ವದಸಿ ಕಲ್ಯಾಣಿ ತತ್ಸರ್ವಂ ಚ ಭವಿಷ್ಯತಿ।  
ಸರ್ವಾನ್ಮನೋರಥಾನ್ಭದ್ರೇ ದಾಸ್ಯಸಿ ತ್ವಂ ಚ ನಾನ್ಯಥಾ॥೧೦೨॥  
ಮಮ ಭಕ್ತಾಶ್ಚ ಯೇ ಲೋಕೇ ಯೇ ಚ ಭಕ್ತಾಸ್ತು ಕಾರ್ತ್ತಿಕೇ।  
---ಶ್ರೀಪಾದ್ಮೇ ಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ ಪಞ್ಚಪಞ್ಚಾಶತ್ಸಾಹಸ್ರ್ಯಾಂ ಸಂಹಿತಾಯಾಮುತ್ತರಖಣ್ಡೇ ಉಮಾಮಹೇಶ್ವರಸಂವಾದೇ ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುತ್ಪತ್ತಿ-ಮುರವಧೋ ನಾಮ ಚತ್ವಾರಿಂಶೋಽಧ್ಯಾಯಃ॥೪೦॥  
  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಫಲಂ ಪ್ರೋಕ್ತಂ ಪಾದ್ಮಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ---  
ಶಙ್ಖೋದ್ಧಾರೇ ನರಃ ಸ್ನಾತ್ವಾ ದೃಷ್ಟ್ವಾ ದೇವಂ ಗದಾಧರಮ್॥೩೫॥  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಸ್ಯ ಕಲಾಂ ನಾರ್ಹತಿ ಷೋಡಶೀಮ್।  
ಸಙ್ಕ್ರಾನ್ತಿಷು ಚತುರ್ಲಕ್ಷಂ ಯೋ ದದಾತಿ ನೃಪೋತ್ತಮ॥೩೬॥  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಸ್ಯ ಕಲಾಂ ನಾರ್ಹತಿ ಷೋಡಶೀಮ್।  
ಪ್ರಭಾಸಕ್ಷೇತ್ರೇ ಯತ್ಪುಣ್ಯಂ ಗ್ರಹಣೇ ಚನ್ದ್ರಸೂರ್ಯಯೋಃ॥೩೭॥  
ತತ್ಫಲಂ ಜಾಯತೇ ನೂನಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ಕೇದಾರೇ ಚೋದಕಂ ಪೀತ್ವಾ ಪುನರ್ಜನ್ಮ ನ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ॥೩೮॥  
ತಥಾ ಚೈಕಾದಶೀ ಪಾರ್ಥ ಗರ್ಭವಾಸಕ್ಷಯಙ್ಕರೀ।  
ಅಶ್ವಮೇಧಸ್ಯ ಯಜ್ಞಸ್ಯ ಪೃಥಿವ್ಯಾಂ ಯತ್ಫಲಂ ಲಭೇತ್॥೩೯॥  
ತಸ್ಮಾಚ್ಛತಗುಣಂ ಪುಣ್ಯಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ತಪಸ್ವಿನೋ ಗೃಹೇ ಯಸ್ಯ ಭುಞ್ಜತೇ ಚ ದ್ವಿಜೋತ್ತಮಾಃ॥೪೦॥  
ತತ್ಫಲಂ ಜಾಯತೇ ನೂನಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ಗೋಸಹಸ್ರೇಣ ಯತ್ಪುಣ್ಯಂ ದತ್ವಾ ವೇದಾನ್ತಪಾರಗೇ॥೪೧॥  
ತಸ್ಮಾಚ್ಛತಗುಣಂ ಪುಣ್ಯಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ಯೇಷಾಂ ದೇಹೇ ತ್ರಯೋ ದೇವಾ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮವಿಷ್ಣುಮಹೇಶ್ವರಾಃ॥೪೨॥  
ವಸನ್ತಿ ತೇಷಾಂ ತೇ ತುಲ್ಯಾ ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ತೇ ನರಾಃ ಪುಣ್ಯಕರ್ಮಾಣೋ ಯೇ ಭಕ್ತಾ ಹರಿಪೂಜಕಾಃ॥೪೩॥  
ಏಕಾದಶೀವ್ರತಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ಪುಣ್ಯಸಙ್ಖ್ಯಾ ನ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ।  
ಏತತ್ಪುಣ್ಯಂ ಭವೇತ್ ತಸ್ಯ ಯತ್ಸುರೈರಪಿ ದುರ್ಲಭಮ್॥೪೪॥  
ಏಕಾದಶೀಸಮಂ ನಾಸ್ತಿ ವ್ರತಂ ಪಾಪಪ್ರಣಾಶನಮ್॥೧೧೮॥  
---ಶ್ರೀಪಾದ್ಮೇ ಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ ಪಞ್ಚಪಞ್ಚಾಶತ್ಸಾಹಸ್ರ್ಯಾಂ ಸಂಹಿತಾಯಾಮುತ್ತರಖಣ್ಡೇ ಉಮಾಮಹೇಶ್ವರಸಂವಾದೇ ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುತ್ಪತ್ತಿ-ಮುರವಧೋ ನಾಮ ಚತ್ವಾರಿಂಶೋಽಧ್ಯಾಯಃ॥೪೦॥

da8fd3c845.b: Observed on Amāvāsyā tithi of Āśvayujaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).

da9190bce2.b: Total lunar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈12.0 of 12 aṅgulas), Moon at the Rahu node (mukha/ascending).
da9190bce2.d: Umbral magnitude: 1.36 (parimāṇa ≈12.0 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 09:06►02:25 (from 3 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra śatabhiṣak/pūrvaprōṣṭhapadā/uttaraprōṣṭhapadā (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or punarvasuḥ (anujanma) or viśākhā (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: kumbhaḥ, mīnaḥ, karkaṭaḥ, vr̥śchikaḥ get more ashubha phala, mithunam, siṁhaḥ, tulā, makaraḥ somewhat ashubha, mēṣaḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ, kanyā, dhanuḥ shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. daec934822.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

This Nayanmar, a Vellala from Tiru Nidur in the Chola kingdom, was renowned for his profound devotion to Bhagavan Shiva and His devotees. Known for his strength and skill in combat, he became a beacon of hope for those in distress, often aiding the weak and defeated. He offered his services as a professional fighter (fencer), setting a wage for his involvement. Significantly, he used the earnings from these endeavors to feed and care for devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, thus earning the moniker ‘Munaiyaduvar’. His life was marked by two key lessons: first, the use of his God-given talent in fencing was always in defense of righteousness, supporting those who were oppressed or downtrodden. Second, he consistently dedicated the fruits of his efforts to serving Bhagavan, aligning with the core teachings of the Bhagavad Gita and various saints.

dc0b0aff48.b: Observed on Anūrādhā nakshatra of Vr̥ṣabhaḥ (sidereal solar) month (Sāṅgavaḥ/paraviddha). The event occurred in 4995 (Kali era).
dc0b0aff48.d: Renowned as Mahaswami, the sixty-eighth Jagadguru was born in the Harita gotra, at a place named Utkṛṣṭa. In Kali Yuga, when 4995 years had passed, in the year Jaya, during the solar transit in Vrishabha, under the Anuradha constellation, in the dark fortnight (Krishna Paksha), at midday on the Pratipat (first lunar day), He was born. Named Swaminathan, He was the fruit of the penance of the couple Mahalakshmi and Subrahmanya. When the two previous Gurus (the 66th and 67th Acharyas) had departed due to illness, by their command, He took up sannyasa at the young age of thirteen. Bearing the sacred name Chandrashekharendra, an embodiment of omniscience, He undertook three pilgrimages across India on foot. Becoming a visible divine presence, He gently drew people towards Dharma (righteousness), and guided the world for a blessed span of one hundred years. In Kanchi, the great sage attained final liberation on the twelfth day of the dark fortnight of Margashirsha month, Shrimukha year, in the afternoon (CE 1994-01-08). The adhishthanam is in the premises of Kanchi Matham at https://maps.app.goo.gl/GqcNJ87GrkU2o4RB9.
dc0b0aff48.s:
ಮಹಾಸ್ವಾಮೀತಿ ವಿಖ್ಯಾತಸ್ತ್ವಷ್ಟಷಷ್ಟೋ ಜಗದ್ಗುರುಃ।  
ಹಾರೀತೇಽನ್ವಯ ಉದ್ಭೂತ ಉತ್ಕೃಷ್ಟೇ ನಾಮ ಧಾಮನಿ॥೨೫॥  
ಪಞ್ಚೋನೇ ವರ್ಷಸಾಹಸ್ರಪಞ್ಚಕೇ ವಿಗತೇ ಕಲೌ।  
ಜಯವರ್ಷೇ ವೃಷೇ ಮಾಸಿ ಮೈತ್ರರ್ಕ್ಷೇ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷಕೇ॥೨೬॥  
ಪ್ರತಿಪತ್ತಿಥಿಮಧ್ಯಾಹ್ನೇ ಸ್ವಾಮಿನಾಥೇತಿ ಕೀರ್ತಿತಃ।  
ಮಹಾಲಕ್ಷ್ಮೀಸುಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣ್ಯದಮ್ಪತ್ಯೋಸ್ತಪಸಃ ಫಲಮ್॥೨೭॥  
ರುಜಾಽಪಹೃತದೇಹತ್ವೇ ಪೂರ್ವಯೋರ್ಗುರುನಾಥಯೋಃ।  
ತದಾಜ್ಞಯಾ ಸ ಸನ್ನ್ಯಸ್ತೋ ವಯಸ್ಯೂನತ್ರಯೋದಶೇ॥೨೮॥  
ಚನ್ದ್ರಶೇಖರೇತಿ ಪುಣ್ಯನಾಮ ಬಿಭ್ರತ್ ಸ ಆಶ್ರಮೀ।  
ಸರ್ವಜ್ಞಮೂರ್ತಿಸ್ತ್ರಿರ್ಯಾತ್ರಾಂ ಭಾರತಸ್ಯಾಚರತ್ ಪದಾ॥೨೯॥  
ಪ್ರತ್ಯಕ್ಷಂ ದೈವತಂ ಭೂತ್ವಾ ಧರ್ಮೇ ಚಾಕೃಷ್ಯ ಮಾರ್ದವಾತ್।  
ಲೋಕಾನ್ ಸಮನುಜಗ್ರಾಹ ವರ್ಷಾಣಾಂ ಶತಕಂ ಶುಭಮ್॥೩೦॥  
ಕಾಞ್ಚ್ಯಾಂ ವಿದೇಹಕೈವಲ್ಯಂ ಪ್ರಾಪದ್ಯತ ಮುನೀಶ್ವರಃ।  
ಶ್ರೀಮುಖೇ ಮಾರ್ಗಕೃಷ್ಣೇ ಸ ದ್ವಾದಶ್ಯಾಮ್ ಅಪರಾಹ್ಣಕೇ॥೩೧॥  
—ಪುಣ್ಯಶ್ಲೋಕಮಞ್ಜರೀ  
ಅಪಾರಕರುಣಾಸಿನ್ಧುಂ ಜ್ಞಾನದಂ ಶಾನ್ತರೂಪಿಣಮ್।  
ಶ್ರೀಚನ್ದ್ರಶೇಖರಗುರುಂ ಪ್ರಣಮಾಮಿ ಮುದಾಽನ್ವಹಮ್॥

dc2e16fd71.b: Observed on Amāvāsyā tithi of Caitraḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti). The event occurred in 4267 (Kali era).
dc2e16fd71.d: Śrīkaṇṭha, son of Śukadevaśharma on the banks of the river Kunḍī (Kunṭī) was a drāviḍa (a southerner), eloquent, wellversed in scriptures and courageous; having received the initiation into asceticism from the compassionate preceptor Bodhendra with the name Śrī Chandracūḍa, He held the responsibilities of preceptorship on earth by remaining in Kāṅci Maṭha. This preceptor surrounded by eminent scholarpoets Maṅka, Śrī Jayadeva, Kṛṣṇa, Suhala, carrying out digvijaya throughout the earth defeated in debate the exponent of Jainism Hemācārya, whose presence embellished the assembly of King Vidyālola Kumārapāla. This preceptor Śrī Chandracūḍa meditating on the mystic syllable that dispels grief/removes misery, adorning the seat (of preceptor) for sixty-eight years, became Videha by giving up the wondrous physical body on the New moon day in Caitra month of the year Pārthiva in the Kali era 4267. This renowned preceptor followed Śrī Jayadeva, Kṛṣṇamiśra, Suhala and others, adored by King Jayasimha and Kumārapāla, destroyed the arrogance of the Jaina exponent Hemācārya and attained the final beatitude at Aruṇācala.
dc2e16fd71.s:
ಶ್ರೀಕಣ್ಠಃ ಶುಕದೇವಶರ್ಮತನಯಃ ಕುಣ್ಡೀನದೀಕೂಲಭೂರ್-  
ವಾಗ್ಮೀ ವಾಙ್ಮಯತತ್ತ್ವಸಙ್ಗ್ರಹಪಟುರ್ಧೃಷ್ಟೋ ವಟುರ್ದ್ರಾವಿಡಃ।  
ಬೋಧೇನ್ದ್ರಾರ್ಯಕೃಪಾಗೃಹೀತನಿಯಮಃ ಶ್ರೀಚನ್ದ್ರಚೂಡಾಖ್ಯಯಾ  
ತಿಷ್ಠನ್ ಕಾಞ್ಚಿಮಠೇ ಬಭಾರ ಸ ಧುರಾಮ್ ಆಚಾರ್ಯಕೀಂ ಭೂತಲೇ॥೯೧॥  
ಮಙ್ಖಶ್ರೀಜಯದೇವಕೃಷ್ಣಸುಹಲಪ್ರಷ್ಠೈರ್ಮಹಿಷ್ಠೈರ್ವೃತೋ  
ವಿದ್ವದ್ಭಿಃ ಪರಿತಃ ಕ್ಷಿತಿಂ ವಿರಚಯನ್ ಯಾತ್ರಾಂ ವಿಜೈತ್ರಾಂ ವ್ರತೀ।  
ವಿದ್ಯಾಲೋಲಕುಮಾರಪಾಲನೃಪತೇಃ ಸಂಸತ್ಸಮುತ್ತಂಸಿತಂ  
ಹೇಮಾಚಾರ್ಯಮಪಿ ವ್ಯಪಾಕೃತ ಗಿರಾ ವಾಗಷ್ಟಕವ್ಯಾಕೃತಮ್॥೯೨॥  
ಧ್ಯಾಯಂಸ್ತಾರಕಮ್ ಆರ್ತಿಹಾರಕಮ್ ಅಸೌ ಶ್ರೀಚನ್ದ್ರಚೂಡಾಶ್ರಮೀ  
ಜ್ವಾಲಾ-ಭಾವವಿಕಾರ-ದೃಗ್-ಜಲಧಿಭಿಃ (೪೨೬೭) ಕಾಲೇ ಕಲೌ ಕಾಲಿತೇ।  
ಆಸ್ಥಾಯಾಸನಮ್ ಅಷ್ಟಷಷ್ಟಿಶರದಃ ಶ್ರೀಪಾರ್ಥಿವೇ ಪಾರ್ಥಿವಂ  
ಚೈತ್ರೇ ಚಿತ್ರಮ್ ಅಪರ್ವಪರ್ವಣಿ ಜಹದ್ದೇಹಂ ವಿದೇಹೋಽಭವತ್॥೯೩॥  
—ಪುಣ್ಯಶ್ಲೋಕಮಞ್ಜರೀ

ಮೇಷೇ ಚ ಗಙ್ಗಾ ವೃಷಭೇ ಚ ನರ್ಮದಾ ಯುಗ್ಮೇ ಚ ವಾಣೀ ಯಮುನಾ ಕುಲೀರೇ  
ಗೋದಾವರೀ ಸಿಂಹಗತೇ ಚ ಕನ್ಯಾಙ್ಗತೇ ದೇವಗುರೌ ಚ ಕೃಷ್ಣಾ।  
ಕಾವೇರೀ ತೌಲ್ಯಾಂ ಅಲಿತಾಮ್ರಪರ್ಣೀ ಚಾಪೇ ಚ ಸಿನ್ಧು ಮಕರೇ ಚ ಭದ್ರಾ

ದ್ವಾದಶಾಹಮಿತೇ ಕಾಲೇ ವಸ್ತವ್ಯಂ ತು ಮಮಾಽಽಜ್ಞಯಾ॥  
ಆವತ್ಸರಂ ತು ವಸ್ತವ್ಯಂ ಮಧ್ಯಾಹ್ನೇ ದ್ವಿಮುಹೂರ್ತಕಮ್।  
ಅನ್ತೇ ದ್ವಾದಶ ವಸ್ತವ್ಯಂ ದಿನಾನಿ ಚ ಯಥಾಸುಖಮ್॥

dcd028f406.s:
ಸುಮನ್ತುರುವಾಚ  
ಷಷ್ಠ್ಯಾಂ ಫಲಾಶನೋ ರಾಜನ್ವಿಶೇಷಾತ್ ಕಾರ್ತಿಕೇ ನೃಪ॥  
ರಾಜ್ಯಚ್ಯುತೋ ವಿಶೇಷೇಣ ಸ್ವಂ ರಾಜ್ಯಂ ಲಭತೇಽಚಿರಾತ್॥೧॥  
ಷಷ್ಠೀ ತಿಥಿರ್ಮಹಾರಾಜ ಸರ್ವದಾ ಸರ್ವಕಾಮದಾ॥  
ಉಪೋಷ್ಯಾ ತು ಪ್ರಯತ್ನೇನ ಸರ್ವಕಾಲಂ ಜಯಾರ್ಥಿನಾ॥೨॥  
ಕಾರ್ತ್ತಿಕೇಯಸ್ಯ ದಯಿತಾ ಏಷಾ ಷಷ್ಠೀ ಮಹಾತಿಥಿಃ।  
ದೇವಸೇನಾಧಿಪತ್ಯಂ ಹಿ ಪ್ರಾಪ್ತಂ ತಸ್ಯಾಂ ಮಹಾತ್ಮನಾ॥೩॥  
ಅಸ್ಯಾಂ ಹಿ ಶ್ರೇಯಸಾ ಯುಕ್ತೋ ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ಸ್ಕನ್ದೋ ಭವಾಗ್ರಣೀಃ।  
ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ಷಷ್ಠ್ಯಾಂ ನಕ್ತಭೋಜೀ ಪ್ರಾಪ್ನುಯಾದೀಪ್ಸಿತಂ ಸದಾ॥೪॥  
ದತ್ತ್ವಾಽರ್ಘ್ಯಂ ಕಾರ್ತಿಕೇಯಾಯ ಸ್ಥಿತ್ವಾ ವೈ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಮುಖಃ।  
ದಧ್ನಾ ಘೃತೋದಕೈಃ ಪುಷ್ಪೈರ್ಮನ್ತ್ರೇಣಾನೇನ ಸುವ್ರತ॥೫॥  
ಸಪ್ತರ್ಷಿದಾರಜ ಸ್ಕನ್ದ ಸ್ವಾಹಾಪತಿಸಮುದ್ಭವ।  
ರುದ್ರಾರ್ಯಮಾಗ್ನಿಜ ವಿಭೋ ಗಙ್ಗಾಗರ್ಭ ನಮೋಽಸ್ತು ತೇ।  
ಪ್ರೀಯತಾಂ ದೇವಸೇನಾನೀಃ ಸಮ್ಪಾದಯತು ಹೃದ್ಗತಮ್॥೬॥  
ದತ್ತ್ವಾ ವಿಪ್ರಾಯ ಚಾಽಽತ್ಮಾನಂ ಯಚ್ಚಾನ್ಯದಪಿ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ।  
ಪಶ್ಚಾದ್ಭುಙ್ಕ್ತೇ ತ್ವಸೌ ರಾತ್ರೌ ಭೂಮಿಂ ಕೃತ್ವಾ ತು ಭಾಜನಮ್॥೭॥  
ಏವಂ ಷಷ್ಠ್ಯಾಂ ವ್ರತಂ ಸ್ನೇಹಾತ್ಪ್ರೋಕ್ತಂ ಸ್ಕನ್ದೇನ ಯತ್ನತಃ।  
ತನ್ನಿಬೋಧ ಮಹಾರಾಜ ಪ್ರೋಚ್ಯಮಾನಂ ಮಯಾಽಖಿಲಮ್॥೮॥  
ಷಷ್ಠ್ಯಾಂ ಯಸ್ತು ಫಲಾಹಾರೋ ನಕ್ತಾಹಾರೋ ಭವಿಷ್ಯತಿ।  
ಶುಕ್ಲಾಕೃಷ್ಣಾಸು ನಿಯತೋ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚಾರೀ ಸಮಾಹಿತಃ॥೯॥  
ತಸ್ಯ ಸಿದ್ಧಿಂ ಧೃತಿಂ ತುಷ್ಟಿಂ ರಾಜ್ಯಮಾಯುರ್ನಿರಾಮಯಮ್।  
ಪಾರತ್ರಿಕಂ ಚೈಹಿಕಂ ಚ ದದ್ಯಾತ್ಸ್ಕನ್ದೋ ನ ಸಂಶಯಃ॥೧೦॥  
ಯೋ ಹಿ ನಕ್ತೋಪವಾಸಃ ಸ್ಯಾತ್ಸ ನಕ್ತೇನ ವ್ರತೀ ಭವೇತ್।  
ಇಹ ವಾಽಮುತ್ರ ಸೋಽತ್ಯನ್ತಂ ಲಭತೇ ಖ್ಯಾತಿಮುತ್ತಮಾಮ್।  
ಸ್ವರ್ಗೇ ಚ ನಿಯತಂ ವಾಸಂ ಲಭತೇ ನಾತ್ರ ಸಂಶಯಃ॥೧೧॥  
ಇಹ ಚಾಽಽಗತ್ಯ ಕಾಲಾನ್ತೇ ಯಥೋಕ್ತಫಲಭಾಗ್ಭವೇತ್।  
ದೇವಾನಾಮಪಿ ವನ್ದ್ಯೋಽಸೌ ರಾಜ್ಞಾಂ ರಾಜಾ ಭವಿಷ್ಯತಿ॥೧೨॥  
ಯಶ್ಚಾಪಿ ಶೃಣುಯಾತ್ಕಲ್ಪಂ ಷಷ್ಠ್ಯಾಃ ಕುರುಕುಲೋದ್ವಹ।  
ತಸ್ಯ ಸಿದ್ಧಿಸ್ತಥಾ ತುಷ್ಟಿರ್ಧೃತಿಃ ಸ್ಯಾತ್ಖ್ಯಾತಿಸಮ್ಭವಾ॥೧೩॥

df45029b2d.d:
The Phalguna Paurnami festival is a grand five-day celebration held annually at the Swami Pushkarini. Each day of the festival features a different set of deities taken for a celestial ride on a beautifully decorated float in the temple tank.

1. On the first day, Bhagavan Rama, along with Sita and Lakshmana, are worshipped and taken for a ride on the float.
2. The second day is dedicated to Bhagavan Krishna and Rukmini, who are also offered puja and taken on the float for a pleasure ride.

For the last three days, from Trayodashi to Paurnami:
1. Sri Malayappa Swami, accompanied by Sridevi and Bhudevi, are taken out for a ride in the temple tank.
2. The third day includes three rounds of the float, increasing to five rounds on the next day.
3. On the final day, the utsava murtis (festival deities) are taken for a splendid ride on the float for seven rounds, attracting a large number of pilgrims. The beauty of the deities is further enhanced by the charm of the full moon, making this day particularly special and visually stunning.

The dvipuṣkara occurs when the bhadrā tithis coincide with the same days as above, but with the dvipāda nakṣatras, which are mr̥gaśīrṣa, chitrā and dhaniṣṭhā. Like the tripuṣkara which gives a three-fold multiplier for śubha and aśubha, the dvipuṣkara has a two-fold effect.
